role.altitude: The programming director keeps editorial judgement, coordination between departments, hiring and reviews; loudness fixing, subtitles, roster building and hours admin shrink.
skills_to_grow: Setting roster rules and file quality profiles that the tools check
role.ambitious_version: A programming director whose rosters, quality checks and hours run on rules, with the week spent on programmes and people.

tasks.short: Review incoming material, write intros and promo copy, edit audio and video to slot length, add subtitles, check technical quality, approve the final item and move it to playout.

steps.what: Programming director reviews incoming packages, news items and promos for the schedule
Programming director prepares copy: intros, links and promo text

loop.input: The package's script, its metadata (title, names, length) and the house style for intros and promos.
loop.output: A draft intro or promo text of the target length.
loop.check: Every name, number and claim must appear in the package script or metadata, or it is marked; the director edits every text before it goes on air.
loop.stop: One draft per package version; if rejected, the director writes it.
loop.why_not_simpler: A template sets length and format, but each intro has to say what this package is about.

steps.what: Programming director edits tape: makes the editorial cuts to slot length and fixes transitions
Programming director levels audio and trims silences
Programming director adds subtitles and metadata to the item

loop.input: The audio track of the edited item and the names list from its script.
loop.output: A timed subtitle file in the station's subtitle format.
loop.check: Names must match the script's names list or are marked; the director plays the item with subtitles and corrects every line.
loop.stop: One transcription per edit; a new edit means a new run.
loop.why_not_simpler: There is no rule that turns speech into text; typing takes several times the item length.

steps.what: Programming director checks technical quality: loudness, format, black or silent passages
Programming director plays the final item through with its copy and approves the material for broadcasting
Programming director moves the approved item to the playout server

approvals.approved_version: item file and copy as played through and approved in s7, identified by file checksum; any re-edit voids it

tasks.design: In the station's editing and media system ({OTHER}), loudness is normalised and silences trimmed by fixed rules, and an automatic file check flags loudness, format and black or silent passages so the director reviews only flagged items. A bounded step drafts intros and promo text from the package script, checked against it, and speech-to-text drafts subtitles that the director corrects line by line. Choosing material, editorial cuts and the final play-through stay with the director; only the approved file version moves to playout.
tasks.previous_blocker: Levels, subtitles and quality checks were done by ear and by hand for every item.
tasks.enabler_now: Media systems apply loudness rules and file checks automatically; Dutch speech-to-text is good enough to correct.
tasks.still_hard: Editorial cuts: what to keep and what to drop.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing what makes an item work on air.

ambition.what: Subtitles on all items for deaf and hard-of-hearing viewers, not only on prime-time programmes.

tasks.altitude: The director spends more time on choosing and shaping material; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Which file checks catch problems that ears miss.

evidence.claim: Broadcast media systems normalise loudness to a set target and run automatic file quality checks.
Speech-to-text tools produce timed subtitles that a person can correct.
AI-made text published to inform the public needs disclosure unless a person reviews it under editorial responsibility.

assumptions: Boundary: from incoming material to the item ready for playout; scheduling and playout are outside.
Input contract for s2: package scripts and metadata delivered with each item by the producing department; fallback is writing from the item itself.
Input contract for s6: the station's loudness target and format profile set once by the technical team.
Every drafted text is edited by the director, so it airs under editorial responsibility.
Choosing material and the final play-through keep their full time.
unknowns: Items per day and share with speech.
Whether subtitles are required for the station's channels.
research_questions: How many subtitle lines need correction per minute?
How many items fail the automatic file check?

already_counted.description: Programming director edits drafted intros and promos.
Programming director reviews flagged quality issues.

incremental.description: Programming director keeps the intro style notes and subtitle format current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: music radio with short links and little speech to subtitle; high: a news and current-affairs channel with many spoken packages.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Hold daily coordination meetings with news, programming and sales, pass on schedule changes, settle conflicts over airtime and studios, keep the shared planning and write the weekly memo.

steps.what: Programming director holds daily coordination meetings with news, programming and sales
Programming director tells departments about schedule changes such as breaking news or sports overruns
Programming director settles conflicts between departments over airtime, studios and crew
Programming director keeps a shared planning spreadsheet of specials, events and coverage
Programming director writes the weekly coordination memo to all departments

tasks.design: Specials, events and coverage are planned in the station's scheduling system ({OTHER}) instead of a spreadsheet, visible to news, programming and sales. When the director enters a schedule change, the system notifies the departments subscribed to that slot, and the weekly memo is generated from the week's planned items and changes for the director to add notes. Coordination meetings and settling conflicts stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: The planning lived in one spreadsheet and changes went out by phone and chat one department at a time.
tasks.enabler_now: Scheduling systems share plans across departments and notify on changes.
tasks.still_hard: Departments competing for the same airtime and studio.
tasks.human_edge: Getting news and programming to agree when both have a case.
tasks.altitude: Less time goes to passing on changes; decision rights do not change.

reach.task: Adjust the commercial log after schedule changes
reach.learn: Whether change notices reach traffic in time.

evidence.claim: A broadcast scheduling product checks rights, repeat limits and content rules when building schedules.
Scheduling systems notify subscribed users when a slot changes.

assumptions: Boundary: coordination between departments for the coming days and weeks; building the long-term schedule is outside.
Input contract for s2: schedule changes entered by the director in the scheduling system; departments subscribe to their slots; fallback is phone.
Meetings and conflict talks keep their full time.
unknowns: How many schedule changes per week.
Whether the scheduling system can share a planning view with all departments.
research_questions: Do fewer departments miss a schedule change?

already_counted.description: Programming director enters changes and planning items in the scheduling system.

incremental.description: Programming director keeps department subscriptions current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a quiet schedule with few changes; high: a news-heavy week with many breaking changes and specials.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Write and approve the vacancy text, have it published, read applications, interview, decide on hiring, and prepare, hold and write staff performance reviews.

steps.what: Programming director writes the vacancy text with HR and approves the final version
HR recruiter publishes the vacancy on the careers site and job boards
Programming director reads applications and selects candidates for hiring interviews
Programming director interviews candidates, often with a test or demo
Programming director decides who to hire and agrees the offer with HR
Programming director gathers notes, examples and goals for each staff member's performance review
Programming director holds the performance conversation, evaluating work performance with the staff member
Programming director writes the review report in the talent system

approvals.approved_version: vacancy text as approved by the programming director in s1; any change by HR goes back for a new approval

tasks.design: Vacancy texts start from a job profile library in the {ATS}, and the recruiter publishes only the version the director approved. The {ATS} shows answers to the director's own fixed questions next to each application, but no model ranks or filters candidates. Notes and goals are kept in the {TALENT} system through the year so review preparation is reading, not collecting; interviews, the hiring decision and review conversations stay with the director.
tasks.previous_blocker: Year notes sat in mailboxes and documents, and vacancies were written from scratch.
tasks.enabler_now: Talent systems keep notes and goals per person; job profile libraries are standard in recruitment systems.
tasks.still_hard: Judging people; using AI to rank candidates or rate performance would be high-risk.
tasks.human_edge: Hearing a presenter's potential in a rough demo.
tasks.altitude: Little changes; preparation takes less searching.

reach.learn: Whether notes kept through the year make reviews more concrete.

evidence.claim: AI that filters or evaluates candidates is high-risk under the AI Act, so the design uses none for selection.
Notes kept on staff are personal data; a system that records them may need works council consent under national rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from the vacancy text to the hiring decision, and from review preparation to the review report; contracts and onboarding are outside.
Input contract for s6: notes and goals entered by the director in the talent system during the year; fallback is searching mail.
No model screens, ranks or scores candidates or staff.
Interviews, decisions and conversations keep their full time; HR time is outside the director's savings.
unknowns: Whether the works council has agreed to notes in the talent system.
research_questions: Do reviews prepared from year notes change ratings or only save time?

already_counted.description: Programming director reads year notes before each review.

incremental.description: Programming director writes short notes in the talent system during the year.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a year with few hires and a small team; high: several vacancies and reviews for a large team.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Collect availability and leave, build the roster, assign programme work, check and send the roster, handle swaps and sick calls, record actual hours and send them to payroll.

steps.what: Presenters, producers and technicians send their availability and leave requests by mail
Programming director collects availability and approves leave
Programming director establishes work schedules: builds the shift roster against the programme schedule
Programming director assigns programme work and stories to staff
Programming director checks the final roster and assignments
Programming director sends the roster to staff
Programming director handles shift swaps and finds cover for sick calls
Staff report actual start and end times and overtime to the director
Programming director records actual hours and overtime for payroll and approves them
Programming director sends the approved hours to payroll

approvals.approved_version: roster and assignments for the period as checked in s5; a later change makes a new version that needs a new check
hours per person for the pay period as approved in s9; a correction after approval needs a new approval

tasks.design: Staff enter availability, leave and actual hours in a rostering tool linked to the {HCM}, with about the effort of today's mails. The tool proposes a roster from the programme schedule, skills per slot and availability, checking rest-time and working-time rules, and the director adjusts it, checks the final version and the tool publishes it. Swaps are requested in the tool, which checks the rules before the director approves; actual hours are compared with the roster, the director approves the differences, and only the approved hours go to {PAYROLL}.
tasks.previous_blocker: Rosters were built in a spreadsheet from mails, and hours were retyped from messages for payroll.
tasks.enabler_now: Rostering tools take staff input, check working-time rules and export approved hours.
tasks.still_hard: Fitting skills and preferences when key people are scarce.
tasks.human_edge: Knowing who works well together on a live show.
tasks.altitude: Hours of spreadsheet work become an hour of checking; decision rights do not change.

reach.learn: Whether approved hours from the tool reduce corrections.

evidence.claim: Rostering tools propose schedules from availability and rules and export approved hours to payroll.
A system that records attendance and hours needs works council consent.
Rest times and maximum hours follow national working-time rules.

assumptions: Boundary: from availability to approved hours sent to payroll; pay calculation is outside.
Input contract for s3: programme schedule from the scheduling system, skills per person and slot kept by the director, availability and leave entered by staff (s1); fallback is the spreadsheet.
Input contract for s9: actual start and end times entered by staff after each shift (s8); payroll gets actual approved hours, not rostered hours.
Coverage: about 80% of staff, including regular freelancers, use the tool; the rest are entered by the director.
Staff self-service takes about the time of today's mails; it is shown in s1 and s8 and is outside the director's savings.
unknowns: Whether the works council has agreed to time registration.
research_questions: How much of the proposed roster does the director change?

already_counted.description: Programming director adjusts the proposed roster.
Programming director reviews hour differences against the roster.

incremental.description: Programming director keeps skills per slot and roster rules current.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: a small team with many freelancers outside the tool; high: a large staff roster with many shifts and swaps.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
